$comment: SQLite SQL oracle (docs/design/oracles.md). `setup` runs first, as the store's own statements; each case's `sql` is a query the store answers. record.mjs runs setup and every case through the native sqlite3 CLI (-json) into recorded/results.json; data-store/tests/sqlite_oracle.rs replays them through the store (Turso) and compares the values. A case whose `gap` is set is one Turso answers differently or not at all: the replay pins that it still does, so a Turso release that closes it fails here and the pin is removed.
setup: CREATE TABLE utf8 (id INTEGER, name TEXT, city TEXT)

INSERT INTO utf8 VALUES (1,'Größe','München'),(2,'Ærø','København'),(3,'日本語','東京'),(4,'emoji 🎉👍🏽','Zürich'),(5,'é combining','Paris'),(6,'עברית','תל אביב'),(7,'apple','Wien'),(8,'Apple','Wien'),(9,'Äpfel','Graz')
CREATE TABLE prices (sku TEXT, price REAL, qty INTEGER, day TEXT)

cases.sql: SELECT 1 AS i, -5 AS s, 9007199254740991 AS big_safe, 42 / 5 AS idiv, 42 % 5 AS imod
SELECT 0.1 AS d, 1.5 AS f, 1e300 AS big, 7 / 2.0 AS fdiv, round(2.675, 2) AS r
SELECT 'grüße' AS v, '' AS empty, ' padded ' AS padded, 'tab	here' AS tab, length('grüße') AS chars
SELECT typeof(1), typeof(1.5), typeof('x'), typeof(NULL), typeof(x'00')
SELECT CAST('12abc' AS INTEGER) AS lead_digits, CAST('3.5' AS REAL) AS r, CAST(7 AS TEXT) AS t, CAST(2.9 AS INTEGER) AS trunc
SELECT NULL AS n, CAST(NULL AS INTEGER) AS ni, coalesce(NULL, 'x') AS c, nullif(1, 1) AS ni2, ifnull(NULL, 0) AS z
SELECT qty FROM prices ORDER BY qty
SELECT qty FROM prices ORDER BY qty NULLS LAST
SELECT qty FROM prices ORDER BY qty DESC NULLS FIRST
SELECT name FROM utf8 ORDER BY name
SELECT city, id FROM utf8 ORDER BY city DESC, id
SELECT id, name, length(name) AS chars, upper(name) AS up, lower(name) AS low FROM utf8 ORDER BY id
SELECT name FROM utf8 WHERE name LIKE 'a%' ORDER BY id
SELECT count(*) AS n, count(qty) AS nq, sum(price) AS s, total(qty) AS t, avg(price) AS a, min(day) AS lo, max(day) AS hi FROM prices
SELECT city, count(*) AS n, group_concat(id, '|') AS ids FROM (SELECT * FROM utf8 ORDER BY id) GROUP BY city ORDER BY n DESC, city
WITH cheap AS (SELECT sku, price FROM prices WHERE price < 10) SELECT sku FROM cheap ORDER BY price
SELECT city, id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM utf8 ORDER BY city, id
SELECT sku, CASE WHEN price >= 10 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS band, iif(qty IS NULL, 'n/a', qty) AS q FROM prices ORDER BY sku
SELECT json_extract('{"a":{"b":[1,2,3]}}', '$.a.b[1]') AS b, '{"x":"y"}' ->> '$.x' AS x, json_array_length('[1,2,3]') AS n, json_object('k', 1) AS o
SELECT date('2024-02-29', '+1 day') AS next, date('2024-01-31', '+1 month') AS overflow, strftime('%Y-%m', '2024-02-29') AS ym, julianday('2024-03-01') - julianday('2024-02-28') AS days
SELECT substr('Größe', 2, 3) AS sub, instr('hello', 'l') AS at, replace('a-b-c', '-', '+') AS rep, trim('  x  ') AS t, printf('%05.1f', 3.14159) AS p
SELECT value FROM generate_series(1, 5, 2)
SELECT group_concat(name, '|' ORDER BY id DESC) AS names FROM utf8 WHERE city = 'Wien'
cases.gap: Turso 0.8.3: ORDER BY inside an aggregate is not supported yet

cases.sql: WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 3) SELECT i FROM n
SELECT id, lag(id) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS prev FROM utf8 WHERE id < 4 ORDER BY id
